text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose modestly today as oil prices pulled back from session highs following reports of potential talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The geopolitical tension that has driven crude prices higher this week — particularly the U.S.-Iran conflict — showed signs of easing, which took some upward pressure off energy markets. Refineries are running at 94% capacity with diesel inventories relatively tight at 107 million barrels, so the company benefits from both operational efficiency and tight product supplies.

The stock's broader picture this week is a sharp decline: it fell roughly 7% from mid-week highs of $424, even as crude oil prices remain elevated above $96. This suggests the market is pricing in real concerns about a potential diesel export ban and its impact on refiner margins — something industry leaders warned about explicitly on September 23rd and 24th. Refiners make money on the spread between crude costs and refined product sales, so export restrictions would squeeze that profit potential even if crude and fuel prices stay high.
